text:
Predicates:
OccursIn(x, y) ::: x occurs in y.
Has(x, y) ::: x has y.
Animal(x) ::: x is an animal.
Mammal(x) ::: x is a mammal.
Human(x) ::: x is a human.
Symptom(x, y) ::: x is a symptom of y.
Fever(x) ::: x has fever.
Headache(x) ::: x has headache.
MusclePains(x) ::: x has muscle pains.
Tired(x) ::: x feels tired.
Flu(x) ::: x has the flu.
Premises:
∀x ∀y (OccursIn(monkeypoxVirus, y) ∧ Animal(y) → Has(y, monkeypox)) ::: When the Monkeypox virus occurs in a being, it may get Monkeypox.
∃x (OccursIn(monkeypoxVirus, x) ∧ Animal(x)) ::: Monkeypox virus can occur in certain animals.
∀x (Human(x) → Mammal(x)) ::: Humans are mammals.
∀x (Mammal(x) → Animal(x)) ::: Mammals are animals.
∀x (Symptom(fever, x) ∨ Symptom(headache, x) ∨ Symptom(musclePains, x) ∨ Symptom(tired, x)) ↔ Has(x, monkeypox)) ::: Symptoms of Monkeypox include fever, headache, muscle pains, and tiredness.
∀x (Has(x, flu) → Tired(x)) ::: People feel tired when they get the flu.
Conclusion:
¬∃x Has(x, flu) ::: No one gets the flu.
